availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

Add dispatch filter UI and default automation eligibility
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KK5P3YQXNQR1MHAHSKA68HE5
Type:      task
Status:    pending
Priority:  1
Automation: eligible

─── Description ───
  The dispatch engine feeds non-eligible tasks (manual_only, needs_review) to agents because:
  
  1. The AgentEditForm UI has no filter editing — dispatch triggers show only the event type, with no way to view or configure filter criteria (automation, tags, priority).
  
  2. addTrigger() creates rules as { on: event } with no filter, and the engine's _matchesFilter() returns true when filter is undefined.
  
  3. Default agent definitions (from kspec setup) lack filter: { automation: eligible } on their rules.
  
  Fix requires three changes:
  
  A) UI: Add filter editing per dispatch trigger row — automation dropdown (eligible/any), tag chips, priority threshold. Default automation to 'eligible' for task.ready and task.needs_work triggers. Show existing filters as badges.
  
  B) Engine: Default to automation: eligible for task.ready and task.needs_work events when no filter is specified. This is a safety net so even unconfigured agents don't pick up ineligible tasks.
  
  C) Setup: Update default agent definitions to include filter: { automation: eligible } on task-worker dispatch rules.
  
  See new ACs on @ui-agent-dispatch (ac-5 through ac-9) and @agent-dispatch-engine (ac-21, ac-22).
Spec ref:  @ui-agent-dispatch
Tags:      web-ui, dispatch, bug
Created:   2026-03-08T02:58:42.044Z

─── Spec Context ───
Agent and Dispatch View
Type: feature
Implementation: implemented
Description:
  View showing agent definitions, dispatch status (running/stopped),
  and active invocations with links to session streams.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: The /agents route

    When: Agent definitions exist in meta

    Then: Each agent shows name, triggers, active invocation count, and completed count

  [ac-2]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The agents page renders

    Then: Dispatch status shows as running with a stop button, and active invocations
show task ref, elapsed time, and link to session stream

  [ac-3]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped

    When: The agents page renders

    Then: Dispatch status shows as stopped with no active invocations

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent definition card on the /agents page
    When: The user clicks the edit icon on the card
    Then: An inline form or modal opens allowing editing of all agent fields (name, description, adapter, dispatch triggers, capabilities, tools, skills, budget, concurrency, auto_approve, prompt_template). Saving persists changes via API and updates the card.
  [ac-5]
    Given: the user is editing an agent's dispatch triggers in the edit form
    When: a dispatch rule is shown
    Then: each trigger row displays its filter criteria (automation status, tags, priority) with inline editing controls — automation defaults to 'eligible' for new triggers
  [ac-6]
    Given: the user adds a new dispatch trigger via the edit form
    When: the trigger is for task.ready or task.needs_work
    Then: the filter automatically includes automation: eligible as the default, shown as a pre-filled badge the user can modify or remove
  [ac-7]
    Given: the user is editing a dispatch trigger's filter
    When: they add tag filter criteria
    Then: the agent only receives tasks matching ALL specified tags — tags are shown as removable chips with an add input
  [ac-8]
    Given: the user is editing a dispatch trigger's filter
    When: they set a priority filter
    Then: the agent only receives tasks with priority at or above (numerically <=) the specified threshold
  [ac-9]
    Given: the user saves an agent with dispatch filters configured
    When: the save request is sent to the API
    Then: the full dispatch rule including filter object is persisted — filters are not silently dropped

toolResponse.stdout:
Agent Dispatch Engine
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KJP27657CZ9AJP5T0XBDEDVK
Slugs:     agent-dispatch-engine
Type:      feature
Maturity:  draft
Implementation: implemented

─── Description ───
Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.


─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits

  [ac-13]
    Given: The dispatch engine builds a prompt for an agent invocation
    When: Task data is available on the state change
    Then: The prompt includes the task title and human-readable trigger context (new assignment, fix cycle, continuing work, or review)
  [ac-14]
    Given: A task.needs_work trigger fires
    When: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
    Then: The last 3 task notes are included in the prompt, each truncated to 200 characters, so the agent can see reviewer feedback
  [ac-15]
    Given: A task.pending_review trigger fires and the task has a review_url
    When: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
    Then: The prompt includes the review URL for the reviewer agent
  [ac-16]
    Given: An agent definition has a prompt_template with {{variable}} placeholders
    When: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
    Then: Placeholders are interpolated with task_ref, task_title, trigger, and review_url values; unresolved placeholders pass through unchanged
  [ac-17]
    Given: A queued dispatch entry is about to be spawned as an invocation
    When: The dispatch engine dequeues the entry and prepares to run it
    Then: The engine loads the task current state and verifies it still matches the dispatch rule trigger event; if the task has moved to a different state, the entry is discarded without spawning
  [ac-18]
    Given: A CLI command transitions a task state while running inside a dispatched agent invocation (KSPEC_SESSION_ID is set)
    When: The CLI would normally post a state change event to the daemon
    Then: The event is suppressed to prevent self-triggering, since the file watcher will independently detect the change
  [ac-19]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running and has been started
    When: A configurable interval (default 60 seconds) elapses since the last reconciliation scan
    Then: The engine re-evaluates all current task states against dispatch rules (identical to bootstrap logic), enqueuing any tasks that match an agent's dispatch trigger but have no active or queued invocation, ensuring that missed or lost events are recovered automatically
  [ac-20]
    Given: The dispatch engine reconciliation interval is configured via DispatchEngineOptions
    When: The engine is created with a custom reconcileIntervalMs value (or the default of 60000ms)
    Then: The periodic reconciliation scan runs at the configured interval, and setting the interval to 0 or null disables periodic reconciliation entirely
  [ac-21]
    Given: a dispatch rule has no filter configured (filter is undefined or empty)
    When: a task state change matches the rule's event type
    Then: the engine defaults to requiring automation: eligible for task.ready and task.needs_work events — only automation-eligible tasks are dispatched unless the rule explicitly specifies a different automation filter value
  [ac-22]

emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.


─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits

    Given: The dispatch engine builds a prompt for an agent invocation
    When: Task data is available on the state change
    Then: The prompt includes the task title and human-readable trigger context (new assignment, fix cycle, continuing work, or review)

    Then: The last 3 task notes are included in the prompt, each truncated to 200 characters, so the agent can see reviewer feedback
  [ac-15]
    Given: A task.pending_review trigger fires and the task has a review_url
    When: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
    Then: The prompt includes the review URL for the reviewer agent
  [ac-16]
    Given: An agent definition has a prompt_template with {{variable}} placeholders
    When: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
    Then: Placeholders are interpolated with task_ref, task_title, trigger, and review_url values; unresolved placeholders pass through unchanged
  [ac-17]
    Given: A queued dispatch entry is about to be spawned as an invocation
    When: The dispatch engine dequeues the entry and prepares to run it
    Then: The engine loads the task current state and verifies it still matches the dispatch rule trigger event; if the task has moved to a different state, the entry is discarded without spawning
